questions.name: Riemann hypothesis
questions.historical_question: Location of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
questions.changed_condition: Alter the admissible function class or symmetry and ask which zero patterns remain stable.
questions.finite_test: Examine a known test class, with a deliberately broken-symmetry negative control.
questions.failure_boundary: Zeros of another function do not resolve the original zeta-function claim.

questions.name: Goldbach conjecture
questions.historical_question: Every even integer greater than 2 as a sum of two primes.
questions.changed_condition: Build a network of prime pairs; retain the target sum and number of paths leading to it.
questions.finite_test: 10 = 3+7 = 5+5; checking even numbers 4 through 200 is only finite evidence.
questions.failure_boundary: Checking a finite interval is not a universal existence proof.

questions.name: Twin prime conjecture
questions.historical_question: Infinitely many pairs of primes separated by exactly 2.
questions.changed_condition: Fix the difference; inspect how pair centers are distributed at changing scales.
questions.finite_test: Use center c=(p+q)/2 and half-gap d=(q-p)/2; compare with O02.
questions.failure_boundary: A coordinate identity cannot prove infinitely many twin primes.

questions.name: Legendre conjecture
questions.historical_question: At least one prime strictly between n² and (n+1)².
questions.changed_condition: Replace average prime density with a bound that guarantees coverage in every local window.
questions.finite_test: Compare an observed statistical count with a provable lower coverage bound.
questions.failure_boundary: Mean prime density does not guarantee a prime in each local window.

questions.name: Bunyakovsky conjecture
questions.historical_question: Infinitely many prime values for admissible integer polynomials.
questions.changed_condition: Reverse the search: identify fixed divisors and forbidden residue classes.
questions.finite_test: For integers n≥1, n²+n+2 is even and exceeds 2; a fixed-divisor control.
questions.failure_boundary: Removing local divisibility obstructions is not proof of infinitude.

questions.name: Odd perfect number problem
questions.historical_question: Does any odd perfect natural number exist?
questions.changed_condition: Describe divisor-sum balance and branch on parity and factorization restrictions.
questions.finite_test: Use the sigma function and residue classes to examine necessary conditions.
questions.failure_boundary: Arithmetic divisor balance is not physical mass, energy, or cosmic phase.

questions.name: Brocard problem
questions.historical_question: For which n is n!+1 a perfect square?
questions.changed_condition: Allow n!+k and classify which offsets k permit a square.
questions.finite_test: Check n=4, 5, 7 for the original +1; study changed k separately.
questions.failure_boundary: Finite known examples do not exclude other solutions.

questions.name: Primes of the form n²+1
questions.historical_question: Are there infinitely many prime values of n²+1?
questions.changed_condition: Vary the constant c in n²+c, keeping other coefficients fixed.
questions.finite_test: Compare residue classes; n²+n+2 is a different two-coefficient control.
questions.failure_boundary: The n²+n+2 example also changes a linear coefficient.

questions.name: Hadamard conjecture
questions.historical_question: Existence of a Hadamard matrix for every positive order divisible by 4.
questions.changed_condition: From exact orthogonality, study minimum defect at each order.
questions.finite_test: A dot product of three signs ±1 cannot vanish; order 4 is possible.
questions.failure_boundary: Matrix orthogonality is not automatically physical field phase.

questions.name: Fermat's Last Theorem
questions.historical_question: No x^n + y^n = z^n in positive integers for n>2.
questions.changed_condition: Allow a third positive summand and classify new equalities.
questions.finite_test: 3³+4³+5³=6³; a changed equation, not a contradiction.
questions.failure_boundary: The changed equation does not refute Fermat's original theorem.

questions.name: Poincaré conjecture
questions.changed_condition: Can the final topology uniquely determine the history of transformations?
questions.finite_test: Construct distinct allowed histories leading to the same final form.
questions.failure_boundary: A final topology does not uniquely store its transformation history.

questions.name: Four-color theorem
questions.historical_question: Four colors suffice for every planar map.
questions.changed_condition: Change the surface, dimension, or adjacency rule.
questions.finite_test: Compare explicit non-planar adjacency systems with the planar class.
questions.failure_boundary: Changing the surface changes the theorem's domain.

questions.name: Kepler conjecture
questions.historical_question: Maximum density of equal-sphere packings in Euclidean 3-space.
questions.changed_condition: Vary sphere radii or the ambient geometry and define new bounds.
questions.finite_test: Use an equal-sphere benchmark before varying size or geometry.
questions.failure_boundary: Packing density is not the author's cycle-density.

questions.name: Mihăilescu theorem (Catalan)
questions.historical_question: 8 and 9 are the only consecutive perfect powers greater than 1.
questions.changed_condition: Vary the fixed difference k between perfect powers.
questions.finite_test: Recover the original theorem at k=1; other k are new questions.
questions.failure_boundary: Different k values define different Diophantine questions.

questions.name: Hilbert's tenth problem
questions.historical_question: No universal algorithm decides integer polynomial equations.
questions.changed_condition: Ask which restricted polynomial subclasses admit decision algorithms.
questions.finite_test: Contrast a solvable linear integer system and general Diophantine equations.
questions.failure_boundary: A restricted solver is not a universal decision algorithm.

questions.name: Squaring the circle
questions.historical_question: Exact construction is impossible with classical straightedge and compass.
questions.changed_condition: Change permitted geometric operations and classify new constructibility.
questions.finite_test: Distinguish arbitrarily close numerical approximations from exact construction.
questions.failure_boundary: A good numerical approximation is not an exact classical construction.

questions.name: Trisection of an arbitrary angle
questions.historical_question: General exact trisection is impossible with an unmarked straightedge and compass.
questions.changed_condition: Permit a marked straightedge and formalize the expanded operation set.
questions.finite_test: Identify which step uses the mark, then compare allowed moves.
questions.failure_boundary: A marked straightedge is an extra permitted operation.

questions.name: Prime number theorem
questions.historical_question: Asymptotic average distribution of prime numbers.
questions.changed_condition: Ask which saved witnesses would reconstruct exact local deviations from the average.
questions.finite_test: Different local sequences can share similar coarse averages.
questions.failure_boundary: An average law omits the fine details of local prime gaps.

questions.name: Four-square theorem
questions.historical_question: Every natural number is a sum of at most four integer squares.
questions.changed_condition: Find the minimum number of summands and preserve the specific representation.
questions.finite_test: Calculate examples and record actual witness tuples.
questions.failure_boundary: Existence does not determine a minimal witness or all representations.
